title_en: Zigs, Zags, and Finding Micro Cap Winners with Ian Cassel
title_zh: Zig 与 Zag：与 MicroCap Club 创始人 Ian Cassel 谈寻找微盘股赢家
subtitle_zh: Ian Cassel 谈在机构缺席的微盘股里，靠管理层与顺风找出十倍股。
description: Zigs, Zags, and Finding Micro Cap Winners with Ian Cassel

turns.en: Welcome to The Derivative by RCM Alternatives. Send it. Hello there. Welcome back. You're listening to Derivative brought to you by RCM Alternatives, where most of us are Barris fans here in Chicago, excited for the season to get started, but we're also excited to be hosting some events in and around the President's Cup here in Chicago.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 RCM Alternatives 出品的 The Derivative。Send it。大家好，欢迎回来。你现在收听的是 RCM Alternatives 为你带来的 The Derivative。我们这边在芝加哥的大多数人都是 Bears（芝加哥熊队）球迷，很盼着新赛季开打；不过我们也很高兴能在芝加哥 Presidents Cup（总统杯高尔夫赛）前后办几场活动。

turns.en: Head on over to rcmalz.com slash gulf if you're in the Chicagoland area to sign up. Onto this episode, where I have to admit I didn't know a micro cap from a micro brewery even though we're a Microsoft shop and I sometimes look at my water in a microscope to see if there's any micro plastics.
turns.zh: 如果你在芝加哥大都会区，可以去 rcmalts.com/golf 报名。说到这一期，我得承认，我分不清微盘股（micro cap）和微型啤酒厂——尽管我们干的就是『micro』这门生意，而且我有时候还会拿显微镜看自己的水里有没有微塑料。

turns.en: So I got Ian Castle on a microphone who's made a career out of working the pink sheets and the OTC markers to find needles in the haystack, diamonds in the rough, whatever you want to call them.
turns.zh: 所以这期我请来了 Ian Cassel。他整个职业生涯都在粉单市场（pink sheets）和 OTC（场外交易）市场里刨食，专门去找那些大海捞针的机会、璞玉浑金——随你怎么叫。

turns.en: So we get into all the micro details. Send it. All right, everybody, we're here with Ian Castle. Ian, how are you? I'm doing great. Thanks for having me on.
turns.zh: 所以这一期我们会把所有『micro』的细节都聊透。Send it。好了各位，今天我们请到了 Ian Cassel。Ian，你好吗？我很好，谢谢你们请我上节目。

turns.en: And it's Ian, not Ian. That is correct. It's Ian. I can't remember if I said this, we had Ian Weiner, Defense Tech on the pod earlier this year and I was telling the story, I think, of my wife had this girlfriend who had her boyfriend and every dinner party, he's like, no, it's Ian.
turns.zh: 而且要念 Ian（伊恩），不是 Ian（艾恩）。没错，是 Ian。我不记得有没有讲过这个：今年早些时候我们请过 Defense Tech 的 Ian Weiner 上节目，我当时讲了个故事——我太太有个闺蜜，闺蜜的男朋友每次参加晚宴都要强调：『不，是 Ian。』

turns.en: I'm like, well, that's just too hard. I'm just going to call you Ian. I'm like, how do you spell it? He's like, I-A-N. Yeah. So I'm glad it's just Ian.
turns.zh: 我就说，那也太麻烦了，我干脆就叫你 Ian 好了。我问：你名字怎么拼？他说：I-A-N。是啊，所以我很庆幸你就叫 Ian，简单。

turns.en: And where do you live? You're in East Coast? Yeah, I'm in Lancaster, Pennsylvania. It's about an hour, hour and a half drive west of Philadelphia.
turns.zh: 那你住哪儿？你在东海岸吗？对，我在宾夕法尼亚州的 Lancaster。从 Philadelphia 往西开车大概一小时到一小时半。

turns.en: So call it, you know, Southeastern Pennsylvania. Are you a Phillies and Eagles fan and all that? I am. Yeah, we're going to a Phillies game on Sunday when they play the Braves.
turns.zh: 所以说就是宾州东南部那一带。你是 Phillies 和 Eagles 的球迷吗，那一整套？我是。对，周日他们打 Braves，我们要去看 Phillies 的比赛。

turns.en: So it's getting- All right, we might have to stop the pod because you've overtaken the Cubs now for the top Wild Cubs pod. I was paying attention to the Cubs.
turns.zh: 所以眼看就要——好吧，我们可能得停播了，因为你们现在已经在外卡榜上超过 Cubs 了。我可是一直盯着 Cubs 的。

turns.en: Yeah. The Cubs and the Braves the last couple of weeks. Yep. And last, yes, last night we banged up Mizrowski and then still lost the game. We got him pushed out and still lost.
turns.zh: 是啊，这几周我一直在看 Cubs 和 Braves。嗯。而且，对，昨晚我们的 Misrowski 挂了彩，结果比赛还是输了。我们把他硬顶上去打，还是输了。

turns.en: I'm like, come on, man. But that'll be fine. I was just listening to another sports podcast. If it's Phillies, if the Cubs can do one and the Phillies two, it's Bears, Eagles come and play the Bears on, I think, Monday night and then that series would be Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday.
turns.zh: 我就想，搞什么嘛。不过没关系。我刚在听另一档体育播客——如果 Cubs 能占一头、Phillies 占两头，那就轮到 Bears 了：Eagles 好像是周一晚上来打 Bears，然后那个系列赛就是周二、周三、周四。

turns.en: Oh, well. So you would be overrun with Philly people in Chicago for four days, which isn't the end of the world. So what happens in Lancaster?
turns.zh: 哦，那也好。那样芝加哥就会被费城人占领整整四天，倒也不是世界末日。那 Lancaster 那边是什么情况？

turns.en: How'd you end up there? Born and raised in this area, I mean, Lancaster, we're kind of known for the, we have the largest Amish community in the United States, maybe the world right here in Lancaster.
turns.zh: 你怎么会落脚在那儿的？我就是在这一带出生长大的。Lancaster 比较出名的地方是——我们这儿有全美、甚至可能是全世界最大的 Amish（阿米什人）社区，就在 Lancaster。

turns.en: So that's kind of what we're known for is Amish. In fact, I think it's like number two in industry here. So it's a, Lancaster is a very, as you could imagine, rural, agrarian, conservative Bible Belt type of county.
turns.zh: 所以我们最出名的就是 Amish。事实上我觉得这是本地第二大产业。Lancaster 是个——你可以想象——非常乡村、以农业为主、保守的『圣经地带』（Bible Belt）类型的县。

turns.en: And it's kind of pinched between like Baltimore is an hour south, Philadelphia is an hour east, and then Harrisburg at the capital of Pennsylvania is like 30 minutes north.
turns.zh: 而且它被夹在几个大城市中间：往南一小时是 Baltimore，往东一小时是 Philadelphia，往北大概 30 分钟是宾州首府 Harrisburg。

turns.en: So we're kind of like pinched in between there. And we still have a train that can take us to Philadelphia, a train that can take us to Manhattan.
turns.zh: 所以我们就是被夹在这中间。而且我们这儿还有火车能到 Philadelphia，也有火车能直达 Manhattan。

turns.en: So I've always kind of liked it here. I hated it while I was growing up when I was a teenager because it's boring, but it's kind of like, once you move away and you're boring.
turns.zh: 所以我一直都挺喜欢这儿。但我十几岁在这儿长大的时候是很讨厌它的，因为太无聊了。可一旦你搬走、自己也变得无聊起来……

turns.en: Boring's good now. Yes, exactly. Yeah. Everything flips amazingly. So. I've always been amazed in the Northeast. Like you get a little bit out of, outside of New York, Philly, and you're in the country super fast.
turns.zh: 无聊现在就挺好了。对，正是这样。是啊，一切都会奇妙地翻转。我一直很惊叹于美国东北部：你只要稍微离开 New York、Philly 一点点，很快就是乡村了。

turns.en: I'm like, right, except for New Jersey, which paved over everything for a hundred miles. Not really if you go to Princeton or whatnot, but right, like how did the Northeast figure that out?
turns.zh: 对——除了 New Jersey，那边一百英里内什么都铺成了水泥地。当然你要是去 Princeton 那种地方也不算。但总之，东北部是怎么做到这一点的？

turns.en: Right. If you go to Denver, you got all these new cities that just keep building, expanding outwards. Who knows? That's for a different podcast, but it always amazes me of like someone had good foresight to say, no, we're going to keep this somewhat rural and not just pave it all over.
turns.zh: 是啊。你要去 Denver，就有一堆新城市在那儿不停地盖、不停地往外扩。谁知道呢？那是另一档播客的话题了。但一直让我佩服的是，当年有人有远见，说：不，我们要把这儿保留成一定的乡村状态，不能全部铺平盖满。

turns.en: So microcaps, you might as well have it tattooed on your head. What's your world? That is my world. That's all I do. I know nothing of microcaps.
turns.zh: 说到微盘股（micro cap），你简直可以把这两个字纹在脑门上。你的世界是什么样的？那就是我的全世界，我只做这一件事。我对微盘股可是一无所知。

turns.en: So we're going to have a little education session here. I'll start with, I'm assuming they're smaller than small caps because they're micro.
turns.zh: 那我们今天就上一堂小课。我先问个最基础的：我猜它们比小盘股（small cap）还要小，毕竟叫『micro』。

turns.en: So I'll let you take from there. Give me the, what they are first, then we'll dig in. Sure. Yeah. And so microcaps, you know, if you looked at the universe of stocks globally, you know, 60,000 public stocks globally across all markets, about half, 30,000 would be considered microcaps.
turns.zh: 那接下来交给你。先说说微盘股到底是什么，然后我们再深入。好的。微盘股是这样：如果你看全球的股票池，全球所有市场加起来大概有 60,000 只上市公司股票，其中大约一半、也就是 30,000 只会被算作微盘股。

turns.en: So microcaps are in every market on earth that there is a market and it's simply, quite honestly, it's just a small business with a ticker symbol attached to it.
turns.zh: 所以只要地球上有个证券市场，那儿就有微盘股。说实话，微盘股本质上就是一家小企业，只不过后面挂了个股票代码。

turns.en: It's usually what they are, but the definition here in the US would be market caps sub 500 million market cap, you know, and that can obviously go down to 10 million market cap and 50, but everybody kind of defines it as 500 million or less.
turns.zh: 通常就是这样。在美国的定义是市值低于 5 亿美元——当然可以一路低到 1,000 万、5,000 万美元市值，但大家普遍把 5 亿美元或以下定义为微盘股。

turns.en: And so it's a, it's a big bunch of, it's a lot of companies, especially here in North America, you know, kind of the US and Canada, it's about 10,000 microcaps that trade in the US and on Canada.
turns.zh: 所以这是一大批公司，数量非常多。尤其在北美——也就是美国和加拿大——大概有 10,000 只微盘股在美国和加拿大交易。

turns.en: It's probably about 60% of all, you know, public stocks and, you know, really the, the opportunity set here is, and the structural advantage in microcap investing is that these are small companies, they have ill liquid, you know, currency, which is their stock, which keeps institutional investors away and that structural advantage has been in place for a hundred years, you know, and all the, most of all the greatest stock pickers from
turns.zh: 这大概占了所有上市公司股票的 60%。而微盘股投资真正的机会集、以及它的结构性优势在于：这些都是小公司，它们的『货币』——也就是自家股票——流动性很差，这就把机构投资者挡在了外面。这种结构性优势已经存在一百年了。史上最伟大的选股人当中，绝大多数——从

turns.en: Buffett to Lynch to Greenblatt all started in microcap and they started here because this is where the inefficiency of this landscape is and it's kind of a, it's kind of a gated city where all the institutions are kept on the outside.
turns.zh: Buffett、Lynch 到 Greenblatt——都是从微盘股起步的。他们之所以从这里起步，是因为这片领域就是市场无效性之所在。它有点像一座有门禁的城市，所有机构都被关在门外。

turns.en: They can only buy these stocks once they perform, go up, become more liquid and allows kind of greater pools of capital to participate, you know, once they become small caps.
turns.zh: 机构只有等这些股票走出业绩、涨上去、变得更有流动性，等它们变成小盘股之后才买得进去——因为那时候更大的资金池才有办法参与进来。

turns.en: And so that's kind of the advantage of a, of kind of the small, astute, even private investors. This is a world where you can gain an advantage because the institutions are kept on the outside even in today's market with ETFs, I mean, you're still talking about companies that trade $10,000 USD a day, you know, and so it's just too hard for anybody managing north of a hundred million dollars to care about this ecosystem.
turns.zh: 所以说，这正是那些小规模、精明、甚至是个人投资者的优势所在。在这个世界里你是可以获得优势的，因为机构被挡在外面。即便在今天有 ETF 的市场里，你面对的仍然是每天成交额只有 10,000 美元的公司。所以任何一个管理规模超过一亿美元的人，都实在很难去关心这个生态。

turns.en: But most of the best, most of the best performing stocks originated out of microcap, you know, so that's the other thing. Are we talking like pink sheet stuff or the figures are too small to be NYSE listed on it?
turns.zh: 但表现最好的那批股票，绝大多数都是从微盘股里长出来的——这是另一方面。那你说的是粉单市场（pink sheets）那类东西吗？还是说它们的体量太小，够不上在 NYSE 上市？

turns.en: Yeah. I mean, the figures I gave you include the OTC on that. But the top two tiers of the OTC, which is a majority of them, I mean, they still have the same regulatory constraints as the NYSE or NASDAQ, they still have to file quarterly filings, they're 10Qs, 10Ks, all those things, they're just an OTC listed company.
turns.zh: 对。我给你的那些数字里是包含 OTC 的。但 OTC 的最高两个层级——那里占了大多数公司——它们面临的监管约束和 NYSE 或 NASDAQ 是一样的，照样要交季度报告，照样是 10-Q、10-K 那一整套，只不过它是一家在 OTC 挂牌的公司。

turns.en: So the OTC is definitely a big chunk of the U.S. percentage of microcaps trade there. And what is that? If I'm on Robinhood, can I pull up some OTC symbol and trade it?
turns.zh: 所以在美国微盘股里，OTC 绝对占了很大一块，很多都在那儿交易。那具体是什么情况？比如我用 Robinhood，能不能搜一个 OTC 的代码然后直接买卖？

turns.en: I don't know if you can on, like, I don't have a Robinhood account, so I'm not sure if you can on the OTC. I'm not sure. Because of FINRA, especially, it's gotten really hard here in the U.S. to be a microcap investor and for the microcap companies that are U.S. focused because FINRA has kind of come down with a hammer and they've kind of labeled everything sub $5, whether you're on the NASDAQ or OTC as penny stock and a lot of those, a lot of the firms and the clearing
turns.zh: 我不确定行不行，我没有 Robinhood 账户，所以不清楚 OTC 能不能在上面交易，真不好说。因为 FINRA 的关系，在美国做微盘股投资者、以及对那些以美国市场为主的微盘公司来说，这几年变得非常难。FINRA 基本上是铁腕出手，把 5 美元以下的东西——不管你在 NASDAQ 还是 OTC——统统打上仙股（penny stock）的标签。很多券商和清算

turns.en: houses just don't want anything to do with small microcap, specifically U.S. listed microcap securities. We don't have that same type of headwind in other markets, like Canada, it's a pretty fervent market.
turns.zh: 行就是完全不想碰小型微盘股，尤其是在美国上市的微盘股证券。在其他市场我们没有同样的逆风，比如加拿大，那是个相当火热的市场。

turns.en: Australia, things of that nature, you know, it kind of gets us to another conversation of like, do companies still go public small? Yeah. And yeah.
turns.zh: 澳大利亚也是这一类。这就引出另一个话题：公司还会以小规模的状态上市吗？会。嗯，是的。

turns.en: The answer is they do. The answer is they do. Yeah. They do still? Yeah. Stick a pin in that one for a second, are the, like, my brain was going to, is this the new private equity or is it the old private equity or something right of like, private equity has gotten so big and they're buying these things before they maybe in the old days would have gone public.
turns.zh: 答案是：确实还有。答案是确实还有。嗯。它们还在小规模上市？是的。这个话题先记一笔放一放——我脑子里冒出来的问题是：这是新型私募股权（private equity），还是旧式私募股权，还是别的什么？就是说，私募股权已经变得这么大，他们在这些公司上市之前就把它们买下来了，而要是放在过去，这些公司可能早就上市了。

turns.en: Like what's your compare and contrast with private equity, which is sort of doing the same thing, right? Small, sub $500 million companies. It is.
turns.zh: 那你怎么对比微盘股和私募股权？后者干的其实是同一件事，对吧？都是买 5 亿美元以下的小公司。确实是。

turns.en: I mean, I kind of divide up the small business investing universe is kind of venture capital, private equity, and then microcap. And the irony there is those first two silos are glorified by the financial media, you know.
turns.zh: 我一般把小企业投资的整个版图分成三块：风险投资（venture capital）、私募股权（private equity），然后是微盘股。讽刺的是，前两块被财经媒体捧上了天。

turns.en: What you hear about is how great they are. The last one, which is ours, we're the ugly stepchild of the bunch that nobody wants to talk about.
turns.zh: 你听到的都是它们有多厉害。而最后一块，也就是我们这一块，是这堆人里没人愿意提的丑小鸭。

turns.en: We're just kind of perceived as penny stocks and the slimy, sleazy wasteland of uninvestable securities. And yet we all are just small businesses that, and quite honestly, ours are at least audited and you can see the financials on like the other two.
turns.zh: 大家就觉得我们是仙股，是一片没法投资的、又滑又脏的荒地。可实际上我们都是小企业，而且说实话，我们这块至少是经过审计的、财报是看得见的，另外两块可不一定。

turns.en: So it's a, it's just, it looks like in terms of funding into like a pie chart, is it, I'm sure it's like 80% private equity, maybe 15% venture, 5% microcap.
turns.zh: 那如果画成一张资金流向的饼图，大概是什么样？我猜是 80% 私募股权、大概 15% 风险投资、5% 微盘股。

turns.en: Yeah. I mean, to give you, to give you an idea of just how big and small the US public microcap ecosystem is, if you were to take all of the microcap companies in the US and kind of roll them up into a ball, the total market capitalization would be probably around 600 billion, you know, which is like what Nvidia makes in an afternoon.
turns.zh: 对。给你个概念，让你感受一下美国上市微盘股生态到底有多小：如果你把美国所有微盘公司揉成一团，总市值大概也就 6,000 亿美元左右——差不多就是 Nvidia 一个下午挣出来的数。

turns.en: Yeah. Or it's like, there's like 20, yeah, probably 20 companies now that have individual microcaps more than 600 billion, you know, that trade.
turns.zh: 是啊。或者说，现在大概有 20 家、对，可能有 20 家公司的单独市值就超过 6,000 亿美元。

turns.en: So, you know, and so that just shows kind of how small it is. And also probably a big reason why we, there isn't much attention brought to the space because institutional capital, there was no reason to arm wave it, you know, on anywhere, you know, but the, but the same structural inefficiencies, you know, that were around 50 years ago when Buffett was slinging cigar butts is still here, you know, today.
turns.zh: 所以这就说明了它有多小。这也大概是这个领域没什么人关注的一大原因——机构资金根本没理由去理会它。但是，50 年前 Buffett 到处捡『雪茄屁股』（cigar butt）时存在的那些结构性无效性，今天依然在这儿。

turns.en: I mean, slinging cigar butts. Well, he was like, yeah, exactly. Everyone's still on the golf course, but yeah, but it's a, it's an area that I got, I got into when I was like 20, I guess I would say 2021 and it's all I've ever done.
turns.zh: 我是说捡雪茄屁股这套。嗯，他就是那样，对，完全正确。大家现在都还在高尔夫球场上呢。不过是啊，这个领域我大概 20 岁就进来了——应该说 2021 年吧，从那以后这就是我做过的全部事情。

turns.en: And yeah, I just think it's an awesome place to invest in. It's obviously has risks associated with it. And you, you kind of learn by losing money, but like all good things in life.
turns.zh: 是啊，我就是觉得这是个特别棒的投资领域。它当然伴随着风险，而且你基本上是靠亏钱学会的——不过生活里所有好东西都是这样。

turns.en: Yep. And so what did that path look like? So when you were right out of college and said, I want to be a micro cap investor. Well, it's odd path.
turns.zh: 嗯。那你这条路是怎么走过来的？就是说，你刚出大学校门就说『我要做微盘股投资者』？嗯，这是条挺奇特的路。

turns.en: There was no guidance counselor that pulled you back. Please, what's wrong with you? Yeah. Said no, go private equity. You need to be on medicine.
turns.zh: 难道没有哪个升学指导老师把你拉到一边说：『拜托，你毛病吧？』有啊。然后说：『不行，去做私募股权。你该去学医。』

turns.en: What's wrong with it? Yeah. I mean, it kind of, it started me a story we're telling it. It all started with my parents when I was a sophomore in high school.
turns.zh: 这有什么不对吗？是啊。这事儿……要说起来得从头讲。这一切始于我父母，那是我上高中二年级的时候。

turns.en: So this would have been 96. So kind of in the start of the dot com bubble technology bubble, they kind of sat me down and said, we save for you $20,000, you know, and this is all you're getting.
turns.zh: 那应该是 96 年，正好是互联网泡沫、科技泡沫刚开始的时候。他们把我叫过来坐下，说：我们给你存了 20,000 美元，这就是你能拿到的全部了。

turns.en: You know, we just want you to know that now so you can make the adequate decision you want to make. And quite honestly, they didn't, they didn't care if I went to college or not.
turns.zh: 我们只是想让你现在就知道这件事，这样你可以自己做合适的决定。说实话，他们并不在意我上不上大学。

turns.en: They probably preferred I didn't because I came from a family business. They would have wished I would have just worked for the family business instead of going to college.
turns.zh: 他们大概还更希望我别上，因为我家是做家族企业的。他们更希望我直接去家族企业干活，而不是去上大学。

turns.en: But I decided that they gave me control over that amount of money and I could be easily incinerated that on a brand new Eagle talent or something like that.
turns.zh: 但我当时的想法是：他们把这笔钱的控制权交给我了，我完全可以一把把它烧在一辆全新的 Eagle Talon 之类的东西上。

turns.en: I had the Mitsubishi Eclipse, which I love the same car, right? I remember thinking about it. I remember thinking about it, but they allowed, they opened up a brokerage account with their financial advisor and put the money in there and put it in my name and it wasn't long until I was starting to get it snail mail from it and they were talking about technology stocks and you know, a month later, I'm like, oh, by $5,000 of that one.
turns.zh: 我有一辆 Mitsubishi Eclipse——我也喜欢那款车，同一款车对吧？我记得我当时想过这事。我记得想过。但他们还是让自家的理财顾问开了个券商账户，把钱放进去、挂在我名下。没过多久我就开始收到纸质邮件寄来的资料，里面都在讲科技股。然后一个月之后，我就想：哦，那买 5,000 美元这只吧。

turns.en: And of course it doubled in like two months and, you know, look at this. Yeah. This is just easy. I've been doing this and then bought another one and then another one, another one.
turns.zh: 结果它两个月就翻倍了，然后我就想：看看这个。是啊，这也太容易了。我就这么一直干下去，又买了一只，再一只，再一只。

turns.en: And so that was like when I was a sophomore and then by the time I was a junior or senior, it was probably 70,000 and you know, I'd gotten bit by the greed bug and I'm like staring at this money.
turns.zh: 那是我大二的时候。到了大三、大四，账户里大概有 70,000 美元了。我被贪念咬了一口，就那么盯着这笔钱看。

turns.en: I'm like, I could spend all this going to a private college at F and M here locally or I could go to the community college and commute from my parents place and get a part time job and not spend any of it and just continue to invest because it's making money is easy, right?
turns.zh: 我就想：我可以把这笔钱全花掉，去本地的私立大学 F&M（Franklin & Marshall）读书；或者我可以去社区大学、从父母家住处通勤、再打份兼职，一分钱不动，继续投进去——因为那时候赚钱太容易了，对吧？

turns.en: So that's what I ended up doing. I ended up going to a local university working for as a branch office administrator for an Edward Jones office in town.
turns.zh: 所以我最后就是这么干的。我去了一所本地大学，同时在镇上一家 Edward Jones 营业部做营业部管理员。

turns.en: So it kept me attuned to the market. So it was basically a receptionist there and then I went to school full time. And then the dot com bubble peaked out 2001.
turns.zh: 这份工作让我一直贴着市场。所以基本上就是个前台接待，然后我全日制去上学。接着互联网泡沫在 2001 年见顶了。

turns.en: My portfolio was about to do a narrator voice. Little did he know the dot com bubble was around the corner. And it was a, the portfolio had a peak of 120,000.
turns.zh: 我的组合当时正要用旁白配音的语气说一句：『他哪里知道，互联网泡沫就在拐角处等着。』那个组合的峰值是 120,000 美元。

turns.en: And then it went down and I went and hit a low of eight. Eight. So yeah, went down to eight. 20 to 120 to eight. 120 to eight and obviously learned lessons during that as well.
But when the other lessons I learned, you know, before that, I thought my next, what I was going to do was going to be become a financial advisor.
turns.zh: 但还有另一课。在那之前，我以为我下一步要做的、我的职业道路就是去当理财顾问。

turns.en: And then just dealing with the emotions of clients down the dot com bubble, down draft, you know, having to answer the phone and stuff like that.
turns.zh: 然后就是要处理客户在互联网泡沫那轮下跌里的情绪，得去接那些电话之类的。

turns.en: I was like, I don't want to deal with clients or customers. Like it's hard enough dealing with my own emotions with investing little and other people.
turns.zh: 我就想：我不想跟客户打交道了。光是应付自己投资时的情绪就够难了，何况还要应付别人的。

turns.en: I said, I don't want to do that anymore. And so basically all those small cap techniques became microcaps. They got baptized into the, the underworld of microcaps and that's where I got introduced to it.
turns.zh: 我说我不想再干那个了。所以基本上，我原来那套小盘股的路数就下沉成了微盘股，算是被『受洗』进了微盘股这个地下世界，我就是在那里接触到它的。

turns.en: And I was right 20, I would have been 21, you know, right around that time. And they're like, what part of you is like, I'm going to go be a dentist or something, right?
turns.zh: 那时候我正好 20 岁，或者说 21 岁左右。那你有没有哪一部分心里在想：算了，我去当牙医什么的吧，对吧？

turns.en: Like, was there a part of you of like, this is stupid? No, I got wiped out. It's, it's weird, like I've been reflecting on that. And, you know, a lot of people say like the biggest educator looking back on their careers or whatever is the losses, I would still point to that first win, even though it was 110 percent luck was probably the biggest, biggest difference maker in my career, even looking back today
turns.zh: 就是，你有没有哪一部分觉得：这事儿太蠢了？没有，我是被清零了。这事儿挺奇怪的，我一直在回想。很多人回顾自己职业生涯时都会说，最大的老师是那些亏损。但即便到今天回头看，我仍然会指向那第一次的胜利——尽管它 110% 靠运气——那大概是我职业生涯里最大的转折点，

turns.en: because it, it just proved that I could make money, whether I, whether I did it with blocker skills, one thing, but I, I already proved myself, I'd made money before and I had enough misplaced self-confidence even after losing 90 percent of my money, but I believed that I could make it back again because I already made money before.
turns.zh: 因为它证明了我能赚到钱——不管我是靠什么技能赚到的。总之我已经证明过自己，我以前赚到过钱。所以哪怕亏掉了 90% 的钱，我依然有那种错位的自信，相信自己还能再赚回来，因为我以前赚到过。

turns.en: And so what was the name of that first stock? Do you remember the first stock that I looked at in earnest was XM satellite radio, which would later merge with Sirius.
turns.zh: 那你第一只买的股票叫什么？你还记得吗？我第一只认真研究过的股票是 XM Satellite Radio，它后来跟 Sirius 合并了。

turns.en: And now it's in every car, but back in 2001, it was a story stock, which just means it had no fundamentals. You know, they just launched a couple of billion of satellites into space and it was actually a stock that was 42 percent covered by shorts.
turns.zh: 现在每辆车上都有它。但回到 2001 年，它是一只故事股（story stock），意思就是它没有基本面。他们刚刚把价值二十亿美元的卫星发射上了天，而这只股票实际上有 42% 的流通股被空头持有。

turns.en: So it was like a huge short position in it. People were betting it going to zero and it was a 180 million dollar micro cap as a story stock.
turns.zh: 所以它的空头仓位非常大。大家都在赌它归零，而它当时是一只市值 1.8 亿美元的微盘故事股。

turns.en: But obviously I didn't care about fundamentals because I was looking at this thing, but I saw that the, the CEO is going to be presenting in Manhattan at a small cap event.
turns.zh: 显然我当时根本不管基本面，就这么盯着这只票看。但我看到它的 CEO 要去 Manhattan 的一场小盘股活动上做路演。

turns.en: And I was a, again, a sophomore in college and I called the conference organizer and they said small cap, not micro cap, small cap of it. It was a small cap event probably because it already XM dip too low by the time they got invited.
turns.zh: 那时候我还是个大二学生。我给会议主办方打了电话，他们说这是小盘股的活动，不是微盘股的。那确实是一场小盘股活动，可能是因为等他们发出邀请的时候，XM 的股价已经跌得太低了。

turns.en: But yeah. Yeah. So I ended up convincing them to let me come to their event and I ended up taking a bus from Lancaster, Pennsylvania to New York City and I couldn't get a one on one meeting with Hugh Panera, the CEO, but I was able to listen to his presentation and I followed him out the back of the room and into his one on one institutional meeting area and had a 10 minute conversation with the CEO and I don't remember what I said.
turns.zh: 不过是啊。最后我说服了他们让我进会场，然后我从宾州 Lancaster 坐了辆大巴去 New York City。我没能约到跟 CEO Hugh Panero 的一对一会谈，但我听完了他的路演，然后跟着他从会场后门出去，进了他跟机构一对一会面的区域，跟这位 CEO 聊了 10 分钟，而我根本不记得自己说了什么。

turns.en: I was just like, my eyes were as big as saucer talking to a public CEO here. You know. Anyway, I ended up taking that $8,000 buying XM at $1.78 per share and sure enough, Lux hit twice.
turns.zh: 我当时眼睛瞪得像茶碟一样——我在跟一位上市公司 CEO 说话啊。总之，我最后拿着那 8,000 美元，以每股 1.78 美元买了 XM。结果果然，好运接连来了两次。

turns.en: They signed, they refinanced their debt the next week. They signed another OEM agreement the next week. Huge short covering rally went from $1.78 to $34 in 14 months, ended up making all the money back from the dot com bubble crash and that's kind of what started my love affair with micro cap investing, you know, from that point forward was, and yeah, it was the fact that I made money then again, but it was more so that an idiot like me could sit across
turns.zh: 他们下一周就完成了债务再融资，再下一周又签了一份 OEM 协议。然后是一轮巨大的空头回补（short covering）反弹，14 个月里从 1.78 美元涨到 34 美元，我最终把互联网泡沫崩盘亏掉的钱全赚了回来。这就是我和微盘股投资这场恋爱的起点。是啊，一方面是因为我又赚到钱了，但更多的是因为：像我这样的笨蛋居然能坐在

turns.en: the table from a CEO and feel like I could gain an informational edge. You know, that sucked me into the, and that's even that at first experience.
turns.zh: 一位 CEO 的对面，并且觉得自己能获得信息优势（informational edge）。就是这一点把我吸了进去，而且这还是我的第一次经历。

turns.en: It's why I'd probably put as much emphasis as I do on management teams and quality of leadership and meeting management, talking to management, visiting them as much as I do today with my investment process.
turns.zh: 这也是为什么直到今天，我在自己的投资流程里，对管理团队、领导层质量、跟管理层见面、跟管理层交谈、去拜访他们，都会投入这么大的权重。

turns.en: And then something you mentioned on the way like things becoming micro caps. Does that, that scares me right of like, oh, I'm catching the falling knife on the way down.
turns.zh: 刚才你提到有一类情况是公司『跌成』微盘股的。这会不会让人害怕——就是那种『哦，我在往下接落下的刀（falling knife）』的感觉？

turns.en: Right. The micro cap is a necessary step before they go bankrupt. Like, what does that look like of like the odds that any of these are kind of a go to zero play also?
turns.zh: 对吧。微盘股是破产前的必经一站。那这种归零的概率大概是什么样的？

turns.en: I mean, I would say a decent, I don't know what the percentages would be that ultimately go bankrupt, but you know, the, the odds aren't in your favor of catching a falling knife in micro cap, especially if it's a money burning business or not in your favor.
turns.zh: 我觉得比例还不低。具体最终破产的百分比是多少我说不上来，但在微盘股里去接落下的刀，胜算是不站在你这边的——尤其如果那是个烧钱的公司，胜算更是不在你这边。

turns.en: Yeah. Correct. Yeah. And all of that would, and it's kind of weird because I got, I kind of got started investing similar to XM where the next five years I would kind of concentrate all in story stocks.
turns.zh: 对，没错。是啊。而且这事儿说起来有点怪：我刚开始投资的方式就跟 XM 那次差不多，之后五年我基本上是集中全押在故事股上。

turns.en: Again, no fundamentals, you know, and, and that's what I would hitch my sidecar to and is like trying to find the next story. The next thing I thought was going to take off because of the story less about fundamentals.
turns.zh: 照样没有基本面。我就把自己的小边车挂在那上面——努力去找下一个『故事』，找下一个我觉得会因为故事而飞起来的东西，跟基本面关系不大。

turns.en: And I would really only start caring about fundamentals, you know, seven, eight years later. And in those early years, met a couple mentors back then, all the activity on these small micro cap companies because no analyst covers them, no institution owns them is was on public stock message boards.
turns.zh: 我真正开始关心基本面，是七八年以后的事了。而早些年我遇到了几位导师。那时候，关于这些小型微盘公司的所有讨论——因为没有分析师覆盖、没有机构持有——都发生在公开的股票论坛上。

turns.en: So we got who finance and raging bull investors up, Silicon investor. That's where retail investors congregated to talk about that. They were the discords of 25 years ago.
turns.zh: 比如 Yahoo Finance、RagingBull、Silicon Investor 这些。散户就聚在那些地方聊这些票。它们就是 25 年前的 Discord。

turns.en: And so that's, that's right. Really went and met some, a few people that would become mentors to me and showed me some things about investing and, and things like that.
turns.zh: 所以就是这么回事。我真的去认识了几个人，他们后来成了我的导师，教了我一些关于投资的东西。

turns.en: And so is there an index, a micro cap index? There is. It's not a very good one. So iShares has the IWC is a symbol, it's the iShares micro cap ETF.
turns.zh: 那有没有一个微盘股指数？有，但不是个很好的指数。iShares 有一只代码 IWC，就是 iShares 微盘股 ETF。

turns.en: And it's just not like a lot of things, the title of it isn't exactly what it is. You know, there's several, I mean, I think it's 1400 stocks in the ETF and maybe half of them are over a billion market cap.
turns.zh: 跟很多事情一样，它的名字跟它的实际内容并不完全相符。我记得这只 ETF 里大概有 1,400 只股票，其中可能有一半市值超过 10 亿美元。

turns.en: There's some that are 10 billion. It's not really the correct representation. But it sounds to me like you're saying you wouldn't, even if you could, you wouldn't want to own all the micro caps.
turns.zh: 有些市值到 100 亿美元。所以它并不是微盘股的正确代表。不过听你这么说，感觉你的意思是：就算你能买下所有微盘股，你也不会想去持有它们。

turns.en: No, I think, I think the worst way, the worst way to get exposure is to own all of them. For the reasons we're talking about, a lot of them don't have a real business or they're on their way down.
turns.zh: 不，我觉得最差的一种获取敞口的方式，就是把它们全都持有。原因就像我们刚才说的：很多公司并没有真正的业务，或者正走在下坡路上。

turns.en: Yeah. Even if you, even if you looked at the historical like since inception of IWC, the iShares, which I think it was back 15, 18 years, you know, it underperforms, you know, by a lot.
turns.zh: 是啊。就算你看历史表现——从 IWC 这只 iShares ETF 成立至今，我记得那是 15 到 18 年前的事——它的表现落后很多。

turns.en: And I mean, it's 78% unprofitable companies, which in today's market works, but not in every market. And so it's just a, it's kind of a cesspool of mainly unprofitable companies, you know.
turns.zh: 而且它里面有 78% 是不盈利的公司。这在今天的市场里还行得通，但不是每种市场都行。所以它基本上就是一个主要由不盈利公司组成的粪坑。

turns.en: So the key to micro cap investing successfully is trying to find actually these small businesses that are real, that are growing revenue profits, and they don't need to raise any money.
turns.zh: 所以微盘股投资要想成功，关键其实在于去找那些真实存在的小企业：营收和利润在增长，而且它们不需要融任何钱。

turns.en: You know, that's something I would learn later on. And what is that? Right. That it almost disqualifies them from being a micro cap because all of a sudden they'll raise money or do a deal and get right launch and have more revenue and quickly move out of that.
turns.zh: 这一点我是后来才学到的。而这怎么说呢？对，这几乎会让它们丧失『微盘股』的资格——因为一旦它们融到钱或者做成一笔交易，就会突然起飞、营收变大，很快就脱离微盘股这个区间了。

turns.en: That's the goal. Yeah. And it's hard to, it's hard to get the escape velocity. Micro cap keeps trying to pull you down, you know, it seems, but, you know, but, but the key really is finding those situations that have good businesses, you know, they're not just a good story, you know, finding a good story with a good business that I can actually earn money that can self fund their growth.
turns.zh: 那正是目标所在。是啊，但要达到逃逸速度（escape velocity）很难，微盘股这个引力好像总在把你往下拽。不过关键真的在于找到那些有好生意的标的——不只是有个好故事，而是既有好故事、又有真能赚钱的好生意，能自己给自己供血来支撑增长。

turns.en: Ironically, ironically, it's the companies that don't need to access the markets. They don't need a bank to raise them money. They just, they just churn higher.
turns.zh: 讽刺的是，讽刺的是，恰恰是那些不需要去资本市场融资的公司——不需要银行帮它们筹钱——它们就自己一路往上滚。

turns.en: I mean, in my world, especially these small micro caps, you know, just the company and it sounds so small, but just a micro cap that can grow revenues from $20 million, which is small, obviously for a public company, $20 million and earn half a million to $60 million in revenue earning five, like that's a 10 bagger in my world.
turns.zh: 在我的世界里，尤其是这些小微盘股——一家公司听起来体量小得可怜，但只要一只微盘股能把营收从 2,000 万美元（对一家上市公司来说这当然很小）做到 6,000 万美元，把利润从 50 万美元做到 500 万美元，那在我这儿就是一只十倍股（10-bagger）。

turns.en: It doesn't sound grandiose, but that's the beauty of micro, like you don't need to find the next Google. You just need to find the next small business that can grow revenues and earnings without deluding you.
turns.zh: 听起来不算宏伟，但这正是微盘股的妙处：你不需要找到下一个 Google，你只需要找到下一家能在不稀释你股份的前提下把营收和利润做起来的小企业。

turns.en: And what give us some examples of some of the stuff some of these companies are doing, like is it boring, like manufacturing type stuff or is it pretty much all the industry types that you find in, you know, small, mid, large, you know, you find down here.
turns.zh: 那给我们举几个例子，这些公司都在做些什么？是很无聊的制造业那类东西，还是说小盘、中盘、大盘里有的那些行业类型，在微盘这一层基本都能找到？

turns.en: I mean, yeah, you're not going to find as many utilities as a micro cap, but pretty much everything else or airlines too, probably, but everything else, you'll see all of those different areas from industrial, new airspace defense, you know, all those areas are represented down here in the micro cap realm.
turns.zh: 嗯，是的，微盘股里公用事业（utilities）不会太多，航空公司大概也不多，但除此之外基本什么都有。工业、航空航天与国防，所有这些板块在微盘股这个层面都有代表。

turns.en: Obviously a lot of med tech healthcare resources, some of the areas that are more prone because they need to raise money might have a higher percentage waiting than what you would find in, you know, a mid cap ETF, but for by and far, you're getting a pretty good mix across the board of different things.
turns.zh: 当然还有很多医疗器械、医疗健康、资源类的公司。有些板块因为天生需要不断融资，权重可能会比你在一只中盘股 ETF 里看到的更高。但总体来说，你在各个方向上都能得到一个相当不错的组合搭配。

turns.en: And so honestly, some of the best micro cap investors I know are just quite honestly small business owners, you know, and they, they have an area of expertise in a niche of an industry and they can dive into, you know, the five or six and micro cap and gain an edge there because they have an understanding of what it is because of their own business or one they used to own or a business they sold.
turns.zh: 说实话，我认识的一些最好的微盘股投资者，其实就是小企业主。他们在某个行业的细分领域有专长，可以扎进微盘股里的某五六只票，在那儿获得优势——因为他们凭自己的生意、曾经拥有的生意或者卖掉过的生意，真正理解那是怎么回事。

turns.en: And so, which sounds a lot like private equity, right? Yeah, exactly. It is. Yeah. And then how, why do they go public? Right. If they're just cruising along, they're not very big.

turns.zh: 对，这是一道非常高的门槛，而且它本来就该是一道高门槛。我没有任何义务去投所有东西。比如：他们的资产负债表能不能扛住一场衰退——但愿别有？就是这些定性的筛选标准。还有：他们有没有我认为优秀的领导层？我把那种领导层定义为 intelligent fanatics（聪明的偏执者），我在这个主题上合著过两本书。

turns.en: You know, I think I can do 25% for the next 10 years.
